title: Absoluteness: bounded formulas and transitive domains

based_on.title: Set Theory
based_on.pages: 76–80 (§18, Definition 18.5, Proposition 18.6, selected bounded definitions from Exercise 18.7, Definition 18.8, Proposition 18.13 and the relative Delta-one consequence); revision 2026-01-31

summary: Prove that bounded membership tests agree across transitive domains, then track which directions survive an unbounded existential or universal block.
abstract: If a collection of sets is transitive, it already contains every member of each set it contains. A search confined to the members of an existing set therefore finds the same witnesses inside that collection as outside it. This observation proves agreement for formulas whose quantifiers are all bounded by sets already under discussion, including tests for inclusion, pairs, and ordinals. An unbounded existential search has a weaker guarantee: a witness found in a smaller transitive domain remains a witness in a larger one, but a larger domain can contain new witnesses. Statements with both existential and universal descriptions agree in both directions when the domains satisfy a theory proving those descriptions equivalent. Finite examples show why these conclusions neither supply missing sets nor make the power-set operation absolute.
